A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multi-subject video-generation work, renamed from ID-Composer to ID-Crafter. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results and component ablations in Tables 1–2, plus qualitative generation, RL and editing results.

after.justification: v4 retains original experiments and adds quantitative RL comparisons, reward and attention ablations, training curves and a human preference study.

M1.justification: The reported attention procedure changes substantively. v1 Section 3.2.1 uses concatenated inter-subject self-attention followed by self-attention over subjects, text and video. v4 Appendix A.1 specifies gated inter-subject cross-attention and residual cross-modal attention, with these blocks inserted in the first 20 DiT layers. This goes beyond renaming or disclosing reward settings.

E1.justification: The same training sources, subject categories, 180 subject-text evaluation pairs and video-editing task are retained. v4 Table S.8 tabulates dataset quantities already reported in v1 Appendix C. New ablations and human judgments do not establish additional data domains or task coverage.

E2.justification: v4 Table 3 newly evaluates offline DPO against online GRPO and the existing SFT/base model. The generator comparators in Table 1 and Figure 4 remain unchanged. The new human study uses existing comparators: VACE-14B, Vidu, Phantom and Kling.

E3.justification: v4 replaces Table 2's Text-Video Alignment metric with Q-Align and changes the reported GmeScore encoder from Qwen2-VL to Qwen2.5-VL. It introduces a five-model, four-criterion human evaluation using 200 questionnaires from 30 participants. The architecture table also revises DiT depth from 60 to 30/40 layers. These are reported setting changes; they do not establish that all retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 provides whole-component ablations and qualitative RL examples. v4 adds quantitative online-versus-offline optimization and reward-component ablations in Table 3, individual attention-stage ablations in Table S.5, mean-versus-minimum identity-reward sensitivity in Table S.7, and training dynamics in Figure S.7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. v4's moving-average training curves and human preference percentages add results without introducing uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v4 newly reports online-RL results of 55.16% Total Score and 66.10% FaceSim, extensive ablation results, and human preference rates of 54%, 60%, 43% and 65% across four criteria. Existing values also change: VACE-14B GmeScore changes from 67.27% to 73.27%, and Ours-14B FaceSim from 60.50% to 60.71%. Revised metrics and configurations prevent treating every difference as a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: v4 adds explicit mathematical definitions for mean/minimum facial fidelity, holistic fidelity, aesthetic/naturalness rewards and gated attention. v1 specifies only a generic quality-plus-identity reward. The underlying rectified-flow and GRPO formulations remain, and neither version presents theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims about multi-subject generation, hierarchical attention, VLM guidance and superior generation quality remain. v4 additionally claims to pioneer online RL for multi-subject video generation and frames its contribution explicitly around balancing identity preservation and motion quality.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations involving credit assignment, online exploration, reward hacking, worst-subject identity collapse and mitigation of copy-paste artifacts. It also changes the computational-cost framing: v1 identifies high cost as a limitation, whereas v4 Appendix E argues that attention overhead is marginal and RL adds a one-time cost. Misuse and dataset-curation safeguards are newly discussed.

D1.justification: v1's reward-calculation appendix is empty. v4 supplies reward weights, noise and normalization settings, and an RL hyperparameter table including learning rate, AdamW settings, batch size and gradient clipping. It revises architectural specifications, states that evaluation data are disjoint from training, reports approximately one-minute inference, and adds a project address. The PDFs still describe model/data release prospectively.

R1.justification: v4 adds targeted references including Identity-GRPO, RAFT, CustomVideo, Vimi, Seedance, Waver and DPO, while removing the earlier VGGT/PartCrafter inspiration citations. It adds a specific novelty claim about integrating VLM reasoning into open-source Wan. The broad related-work organization and principal competing approaches remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and method motivations are extensively rewritten around VLM-grounded online RL. The model and title are renamed, author information changes, editing is folded into the analysis section, and the supplement is reorganized with an overview and additional subsections. The earlier LLM-writing declaration is removed.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. The teaser and several pipeline, dataset and prompt illustrations are redesigned; existing qualitative figures are resized or relocated. New displays include RL and sensitivity tables, training curves and preference charts. v1 Figures 7–10 survive as v4 Figures S.9–S.12 rather than constituting new analyses.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially addresses v1's underdocumented and weakly tested RL component: the empty reward appendix becomes a concrete specification, supported by DPO comparisons, reward/stage ablations, sensitivity analysis and human evaluation. This materially improves reproducibility and empirical support. Remaining weaknesses temper the gains: uncertainty is still unreported, and broad improvement claims overlook Table 1's lower motion, GmeScore and NaturalScore after RL.
